title: Stepping stones
statement:
There are n stones in a row, numbered 0 to n-1. You start on stone 0.
Stone i has a number a_i: from it you may jump forward any distance from 1 up to a_i (or not at all if a_i = 0).
Can you reach stone n-1? Print YES or NO.

Input: first line n, second line n integers a_0 ... a_{n-1}.
Output: YES or NO.
Limits: 1 <= n <= 200000, 0 <= a_i <= 10^9.

Example: 3 2 1 0 4  ->  NO

rubric.key_insight: Sweep left to right keeping the furthest index reachable so far. If you ever stand on an index beyond that furthest reach, you are stuck. You don't need to simulate individual jumps. Greedy on 'furthest reach' is correct because reachable positions form a prefix.
accepted_approaches: DP/BFS over positions with an optimisation (plain DP is O(n^2) and too slow)
work backwards keeping the leftmost good position
edge_cases: a zero in the middle can be jumped over if an earlier stone reaches past it
zeros that form an uncrossable wall
common_wrong: answering NO whenever any zero exists

reference:
import sys
def main():
    d = sys.stdin.read().split(); n = int(d[0]); a = list(map(int, d[1:1+n]))
    far = 0
    for i in range(n):
        if i > far: print('NO'); return
        far = max(far, i + a[i])
    print('YES')
main()
